data.reasoning: The deepseek model completed a thorough review of all AUR repository files (PKGBUILD, .gitignore, .SRCINFO) and found no security issues. The package is a standard VCS icon theme that clones from the official GitHub repository (erikdubois/surfn-luv), installs icon files, and performs reasonable cleanup (deleting .sh scripts and cache files to avoid shipping build artifacts). No malicious code, obfuscation, or suspicious network operations were detected. The qwen model's inconclusive verdict was due to API errors (HTTP 400), not security concerns, and its initial PKGBUILD audit also found the package safe. No .install hooks or patches were present to review.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by tool failures, not security concerns. The qwen model encountered HTTP 400 API errors when attempting to review PKGBUILD and .gitignore files, resulting in an inconclusive verdict despite its initial PKGBUILD audit finding no issues. The deepseek model completed a full review without errors and found the package safe. The openrouter advisory report also found no issues but had a parsing error for the PKGBUILD decision.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to complete review due to API errors (HTTP 400) for PKGBUILD and .gitignore files
learnings: API errors should be handled gracefully to avoid inconclusive verdicts when the model could have provided a valid assessment
Initial PKGBUILD audits that succeed should be preserved and used as the verdict even if subsequent file reviews fail due to tool errors
Model output parsing should be more robust to handle variations in response format (openrouter failed to parse 'User Safety: safe' as a valid decision)
